Okuniew Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Okuniew, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Okuniew developed from the late 19th century; the town was home to Abraham Ostrzeg, an avant-garde sculptor known for Jewish cemetery monuments in Warsaw and Łódź. By 1921, 498 Jews made up 26% of the population, deported to the Warsaw Ghetto in March 1942 and mostly murdered at Treblinka. The cemetery was likely established in the mid-19th century. During WWII, Germans carried out executions here and buried the victims; locals later took tombstones for building material and windowsills. Poland formally closed the cemetery in 1964. Since 2001, students from two local schools and a volunteer club ('Klub Ośmiu') have carried out periodic cleanup work.
